articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

US signs landmark nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia

Sign up for the Breaking News US email

A reminder that my colleagues are covering the latest out of the Middle East at our dedicated live blog.
Donald Trump took to Truth Social a short while and noted that the US will destroy one bridge or power plant, including those near Tehran, “any time” that Iran “shoots a ship” in the strait of Hormuz. 
 Continue reading...
articles.title: House Democrat calls for congressional hearings on Trump administration’s nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia – as it happened

articles.author: Josh Butler
articles.description:
National emergency test alert will be sent to all mobile devices on 27 July, with domestic violence advocates advising how to turn off safe phones

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Virtually every phone in the country will blare an emergency siren at 2pm AEST on Monday 27 July as part of the first Australia-wide test of a new national warning system called AusAlert.
Most phones, and some smartwatches and tablets, will receive a pop-up notification and an alert sound that cannot be silenced – even if your device is on “do not disturb” or silent mode.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: AusAlert test date and time: emergency warning siren will blast over most phones in Australia on Monday. Here’s what to know

articles.author: Roque Planas and agency
articles.description:
Shooting happened on street in popular neighborhood lined with restaurants, bars, shops and homes 
A police officer in Madison, Wisconsin, shot and killed a man Wednesday in an incident that was captured on cellphone footage, sparking local protests.
John Patterson, the Madison police chief, acknowledged the shooting at a news conference, but stressed footage circulating was just one perspective of what happened.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Police officer fatally shoots man in Madison, Wisconsin, sparking protests

articles.author: Maya Yang and Patrick Wintour
articles.description:
Trump administration hails agreement, which comes as the US fights a war with Iran in part to prevent Tehran enriching uranium domestically
The US has signed a landmark nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia that could allow the kingdom to enrich uranium in the future.
In a statement on Wednesday, the US Department of Energy said its secretary, Chris Wright, and his Saudi counterpart, Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman, signed a “peaceful nuclear cooperation agreement”, along with a “bilateral safeguards agreement”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US signs landmark nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia that could pave the way for domestic nuclear enrichment

articles.author: Uwa Ede-Osifo in Los Angeles
articles.description:
Gory details about tarp, mats and inflatable pool come to light during hearing over death of Celeste Rivas Hernandez
At singer D4vd’s former Hollywood Hills home, law enforcement detected possible bloodstains – invisible to the naked eye – on items including a green tarp, black rubber mats and a crumpled inflatable pool that had the odor of fresh laundry.
The gory details came to light on Wednesday, the second day of a hearing to determine whether there was probable cause for the musician, whose full name is David Anthony Burke, to stand trial for the murder and sexual abuse of Celeste Rivas Hernandez.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Possible bloodstains were detected at D4vd’s home, law enforcement testify

articles.author: George Chidi in Marietta, Georgia
articles.description:
President visits swing state to promote ‘Trump accounts’ and says high prices lingering from Joe Biden’s presidency 
Donald Trump scoffed at the word “affordability” as a political message, describing it at a campaign rally on Wednesday as a term concocted by Democratic political consultants to criticize his presidency. Yet even as the president dismissed the notion of affordability, he devoted much of his speech at Wheeler high school to touting the bread-and-butter benefits of his economic policies.
“So I just want you to remember that if you’re paying a little bit more – a lot of it’s come down now, we got it coming down very rapidly actually,” Trump said in Marietta, an Atlanta suburb, casting higher prices today as a lingering effect of the Biden administration.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump scoffs at ‘affordability’ as he touts economic policies at Georgia rally

articles.author: Aamna Mohdin and Jayni Makwana
articles.description:
More than 70 attacks have been recorded over past year, including acts of violence, property damage and vandalism
One mosque is attacked in Britain every five days, according to new data released by the government’s partner for monitoring anti-Muslim hatred.
More than 70 attacks on mosques in the UK have been recorded over the past year, which include acts of intimidation, violence, property damage, harassment, anti-Muslim hate speech, online abuse and vandalism.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: One UK mosque attacked ‘every five days’, says British Muslim Trust

articles.author: Robyn Vinter
articles.description:
New prime minister has made Sarwar – the first senior Labour figure to call for Keir Starmer’s resignation – a peer
Scottish Labour’s rivals in Holyrood have slammed Anas Sarwar’s shock decision to resign as leader to sit in Andy Burnham’s new government, calling him a “chancer” and accusing him of lying to voters.
The prime minister has made Sarwar – who was the first senior Labour figure to call for Keir Starmer to resign – a peer and given him a ministerial post at the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade, No 10 announced on Wednesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Scottish Labour’s rivals decry ‘chancer’ Anas Sarwar for resigning to join Andy Burnham’s government

articles.author: Lucy Campbell (now); Hayden Vernon, Tom Ambrose, Vivian Ho and Mark Saunokonoko (earlier)
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.
The Jordanian army said it intercepted four Iranian missiles on Wednesday with two additional missile falling in an open area, AFP reports.
The two missiles that the army did not intercept fell in “two remote, uninhabited areas, without causing any human casualties or material damage” the army said in a statement.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Iran warns of ‘eye for an eye’ response if US follows through on Trump’s threats to destroy infrastructure – as it happened

articles.author: Hayden Vernon
articles.description:
European Commission says Paramount Skydance’s decision to end Universal venture addresses merger concerns
Paramount Skydance’s £80bn takeover of Warner Brothers took a step closer to being realised after it won conditional approval from the European Union.
The European Commission said Paramount’s offer to ⁠end a film ⁠distribution ​joint venture with Universal Pictures addressed its concerns over the potential merger. As part of its commitments in the EU, Paramount has 13 months from the date of closing the deal to pull out from the venture.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Paramount’s £80bn takeover of Warner Brothers a step closer after EU approval

articles.author: Rajeev Syal and Alexandra Topping
articles.description:
PM says he wants to ensure ‘everything has been looked at’ amid outrage at policy from family of PC Andrew Harper
Andy Burnham is immersed in a deepening political row after ordering a review of plans for the early release of thousands of killers, rapists and sex offenders from prison in September.
After the family of PC Andrew Harper expressed outrage that his killers may be eligible for release, the prime minister responded by pledging to make sure that “everything has been looked at again” before a fresh tranche of about 6,000 offenders were freed on tags.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham stirs up political row with review of release plans for violent criminals

articles.author: Luke Harding in Dnipro
articles.description:
Campaigners in Ukraine pledge to continue nationwide protests until Mykhailo Fedorov gets his job back 
Volodymyr Zelenskyy was under growing pressure to reinstate his sacked defence minister on Wednesday, after campaigners said they would continue indefinite nationwide protests until Mykhailo Fedorov got his job back.
On Tuesday, Zelenskyy bowed to public demands by firing Ukraine’s commander-in-chief Oleksandr Syrskyi. He appointed Mykhailo Drapatyi as the new head of the country’s armed forces, as part of a radical reshuffle of the top military command.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Zelenskyy under growing pressure to reinstate sacked defence minister

articles.author: Jamie Grierson and Kim Willsher
articles.description:
Public prosecutor for the region said suspect had been initially arrested shortly after the murder on 29 April last year
A 70-year-old woman has been charged with the murder of Karen Carter, the British expat found dead in south-western France last year.
The woman was charged on 2 July with Carter’s murder in Trémolat, in the Dordogne, and is “under judicial supervision”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Woman, 70, charged with murder of British expat Karen Carter in France

articles.author: Alice Speri
articles.description:
Mamdani admits he lacks power to arrest Israeli prime minister after saying he’s ‘not welcome’ in New York City
Zohran Mamdani, the New York City mayor, doubled down on his support for the international criminal court (ICC) on Wednesday and called on federal authorities to execute the court’s warrant for Benjamin Netanyahu’s arrest should he visit the city in the fall.
“I call on the federal government to join the international criminal court and to execute both this warrant as well as any warrant the international criminal court holds,” Mamdani told reporters at a press conference on Wednesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mamdani says he can’t arrest Netanyahu as mayor and urges US to enforce ICC warrant

articles.author: Olivia Bowden and agencies
articles.description:
Trump’s 50% tariff threat means there will be no ribbon-cutting celebration of Gordie Howe International Bridge
A planned joint US-Canada ceremony on Friday celebrating the opening of the Gordie Howe International Bridge connecting Detroit and Windsor, Ontario, is no longer expected to take place after Donald Trump announced a 50% tariff on most Canadian goods.
In announcing the tariffs, the president accused Canada of unfairly discriminating against US automobiles, alcohol and dairy products, escalating tensions with one of the United States’ closest allies.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Canada cancels joint bridge-opening celebration with US amid trade tensions

articles.author: Jakub Krupa
articles.description:
Brussels talks between senior diplomats now underway in attempt to sign off 21st package of sanctions, after previous failed attempts 
The Venice Biennale said it would challenge a European Union decision to withdraw a €2 ⁠million grant in response to the return of Russia to its 2026 edition, despite continuing aggression on Ukraine, Reuters reported.
The Italian government sharply criticised the move, while the European Commission warned it ​would suspend or terminate funding if the Russian ‌pavilion returned.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: New Ukraine army chief vows to step up counteroffensive as EU bids to finalise fresh Russia sanctions – as it happened

articles.author: Jon Henley, Europe correpondent
articles.description:
Figures come as large parts of southern Europe endure another record-breaking period of extreme temperatures
France recorded more than 5,700 excess deaths during its June heatwave, authorities have said, as swathes of southern Europe continue to endure another record-breaking period of extreme temperatures.
The French national health agency said on Wednesday that it had recorded 5,764 excess deaths ⁠between ​17 June and 2 July, an excess mortality rate of 36%.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: France records more than 5,700 excess deaths during June heatwave

articles.author: Luca Ittimani
articles.description:
The companies hope to follow in the footsteps of SpaceX, which raised $86bn and soared to a $2.1tn valuation after it listed on public markets in June

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Top US AI developers Anthropic and OpenAI cheered when Australia announced it would set new AI rules.
Big tech celebrating limits on their Silicon Valley VC-funded free-for-all might seem counterintuitive but there’s a much broader play than just what happens in one relatively small market.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why are OpenAI and Anthropic cheering on regulation in Australia? The answer has global reach

articles.author: Tory Shepherd
articles.description:
Military and SES personnel being taught analog communication and navigation techniques as experts warn solar flare could knock out ‘critical space infrastructure’

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia’s emergency services and military personnel are being trained to read paper maps, navigate without GPS support and sail by the stars in case something knocks out the nation’s space capabilities.
A panel at the 19th Australian Space Forum in Adelaide on Wednesday was asked to consider what would happen “if we suddenly lost access to critical space infrastructure – no satellites, no GPS, no remote sensing, no secure communications?”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How will Australia’s emergency services cope if satellites go down? With a sextant and a street directory

articles.author: Donna Lu
articles.description:
Research identifies 808,585 viral genomes belonging to what scientists estimate to be 362,802 different viruses

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

More than a decade after the human microbiome was comprehensively mapped, scientists have now identified the vast communities of microbes that make up the Great Barrier Reef.
Analysing DNA from seawater samples of 48 reefs, researchers have mapped the microbiome of the Great Barrier Reef, documenting more than 360,000 distinct viruses as well as more than 500 new bacterial species not previously known to science.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Great Barrier Reef microbiome mapped as researchers discover 500 bacterial species previously unknown to science

articles.author: Jon Henley
articles.description:
The new PM talks less about the continent than his predecessor, but his agenda is more closely aligned with the EU’s
• Don’t get This Is Europe delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
Europe’s leaders queued up this week to welcome Andy Burnham as Britain’s seventh prime minister since the Brexit vote – all expressing the hope that his tenure would continue the thaw in EU-UK relations initiated by his predecessor, Keir Starmer.
Ursula von der Leyen, the European Commission chief, said she was looking forward to strengthening cross-Channel ties, adding that a “very good” first discussion had confirmed a common commitment to “bringing the EU and UK closer and closer”. France’s Emmanuel Macron said he hoped for a deeper relationship that gave “new momentum to the partnership” between the EU and the UK. Germany’s Friedrich Merz said he, too, was looking forward to forging an even closer bond.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ​Andy Burnham’s ​domestic ​revolution ​could ​unobtrusively pull Britain ​closer to Europe

articles.author: Joanna Partridge
articles.description:
Record June temperatures expected to cut grain harvest by 9m tonnes to its lowest level since 2018 
The heatwave that swept across Europe in June is estimated to have cost the continent’s grain farmers €2bn (£1.7bn) in lost revenue and destroyed 9m tonnes of crops, sparking concern about the impact on the price of food.
Coceral, the European cereals and oilseeds trade association, made the estimate for the harvest of crops such as wheat, barley, maize and oats following the heatwave.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Food price fears after Europe’s heatwave destroys estimated €2bn of crops

articles.author: Tiago Rogero South America correspondent
articles.description:
US secretary of state says international community should ‘join forces’ against authoritarian Ortega regime
Nicaragua’s congress, controlled by the country’s long-serving president, Daniel Ortega, has announced a “work plan” to implement the authoritarian leader’s order that the country should no longer hold elections.
The UN and the US strongly condemned Sunday’s announcement by Ortega, who has been in power since 2007 and, after a controversial constitutional change last year, now governs alongside his wife, Rosario Murillo, as “co-president”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nicaragua’s congress announces ‘work plan’ to suspend elections

articles.author: Emma Bryce
articles.description:
Researchers listening off the Caribbean island of Dominica found variations in the mammals’ audible clicks when marine traffic was close
Sperm whales produce a specific pattern of clicking noises when they hear the noise of boats, researchers have found. The pattern is so distinct that the scientists who identified it said they can now use it to predict when ships are nearby.
Researchers from Project Ceti (the Cetacean Translation Initiative), a non-profit research organisation working to decode sperm whale communication, spent four years tuning in on the calls of 15 sperm whales off the coast of Dominica.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sperm whales change ‘vowel’ sounds when boats are nearby, scientists discover

articles.author: Danny Vincent
articles.description:
Isabel Rose, 26, sentenced to six years for blackmail and perverting course of public justice over her allegations against British man
A British woman who reported being raped to police in Hong Kong has been sentenced to six years in prison for blackmail and perverting the course of public justice.
Isabel Rose, 26, from south-east London, travelled to Hong Kong in early 2024 to visit a British banker she had met while travelling in south-east Asia.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British woman jailed in Hong Kong for blackmail after accusing banker of rape

articles.author: Sarah Basford Canales and Luca Ittimani
articles.description:
Foreign minister Penny Wong will deliver speech criticising China’s recent launch of a nuclear-capable submarine-launched missile

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Penny Wong will warn China that Australia and other neighbouring nations will not be bullied by its “provocative” actions, after its involvement in another “destabilising and dangerous” incident this week.
The foreign affairs minister – who will deliver the address on Thursday in the Philippines, where the 59th Asean foreign minister’s meeting is being held – will also caution world leaders against placing a toll on the strait of Hormuz after both Iran and the US threatened to do amid the protracted conflict.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia to warn China it won’t be bullied by ‘provocative‘ actions as it builds military and nuclear arsenal

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Proceedings suspended as politicians call for Modi government to address police violence and education scandals
India’s opposition parties have shut down parliament in a protest calling for the resignation of the education minister, in solidarity with the new youth-led “cockroach” movement.
Opposition politicians, led by the Congress party leader Rahul Gandhi, gathered outside the parliament building in Delhi on Wednesday, many dressed in black and waving placards calling on Dharmendra Pradhan to quit.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Opposition parties shut down Indian parliament in solidarity with ‘cockroach’ protests

articles.author: Raphael Rashid
articles.description:
Prosecutors seek a one-year sentence and heavy fine after chef garnished dish with insects not approved for consumption
Prosecutors in South Korea have asked a court to sentence the owner of a Michelin-starred restaurant to one year in prison for serving a dessert topped with ants, an insect not approved for consumption under local food safety law.
The request, made on Monday, also sought a 20m won (£10,108) fine for the company that runs the restaurant, Yonhap news agency reported.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Michelin-starred restaurant owner in South Korea faces jail over ant dessert

articles.author: Robert Mackey
articles.description:
New York mayor admits he does not have authority to arrest Netanyahu, adding Israeli PM is ‘architect of a horrific genocide’
Zohran Mamdani, the New York City mayor, acknowledged on Tuesday he does not have the authority to arrest Benjamin Netanyahu, but urged US federal authorities to do so if the Israeli prime minister visits the US later this year.
“Benjamin Netanyahu is a war criminal, the architect of a horrific genocide against the Palestinian people,” Mamdani said in a video posted to social media.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mamdani urges US government to arrest Netanyahu if Israeli PM visits US

articles.author: Hettie O'Brien
articles.description:
In today’s newsletter: ​A White House operating without expertise, strategy or restraint ​is stuck in a conflict with no easy way out, which is sending economic shockwaves far beyond its own borders
Good morning. Within two hours of entering No 10 on Monday afternoon, Andy Burnham had his first call with Donald Trump. After chit-chatting about the football (both agreed England had an “excellent tournament”) and Manchester (our new prime minister invited the president to visit the city Trump once described as a “town”), they got on to far trickier territory: the strait of Hormuz.
The US has attacked Iran for the eleventh consecutive night, hitting aircraft hangars and drone storage sites across the country. It came after Iran launched retaliatory strikes on US air bases and neighbouring Gul…
articles.title: Wednesday briefing: How Trump’s Iran gamble has produced a crisis reshaping the global order

articles.author: Gavin Blair in Tokyo
articles.description:
In April Japan coined new term kokushobi for days above 40C as country advises workers to wear shorts to the office to cope with stifling heat
Japan logged its first official kokushobi or “cruelly hot day” on Tuesday since the new term for when temperatures top 40 degrees Celsius was introduced in April. The Japan Meteorological Agency coined the new designation to warn the public of the heat dangers of days that were once freak weather events but have now become more common.
The central Japan cities of Gujo and Tajimi in Gifu prefecture, along with Toyota in Aichi prefecture, all hit 40C. Gujo’s 40C and Toyota’s 40.1C were all-time highs recorded at their respective weather stations.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Japan records its first ‘cruelly hot day’ as cities swelter in 40-degree heat

articles.author: Robert Mackey, Shrai Popat, Maya Yang and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

Sign up for US Breaking News email

US gas prices have continued to rise since the conflict with Iran resumed this month. According to the American Automobile Association (AAA), a gallon of fuel is now just over $4 – almost a dollar more than a year ago.
It comes as Brent Crude, the international oil benchmark, is now up by almost 2% to $90.92 a barrel.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump announces new tariffs on generic drugs to take effect in 2028 – as it happened

articles.author: Nadeem Badshah
articles.description:
UK resident was evacuated from Democratic Republic of the Congo where there is an outbreak of the disease
A humanitarian worker is being monitored at a specialist hospital in London after potential exposure to the Ebola virus.
The UK resident was medically evacuated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) where the worker had been treating patients with the disease, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Health worker monitored for Ebola in London hospital after working in DRC

articles.author: Shrai Popat in Washington
articles.description:
Mark Carney says Canada is ‘united’ in face of threats as leaders agree to talk before tariffs take effect next month

Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

Donald Trump has defended his new 50% tariffs on most Canadian goods, claiming the country cannot survive without the US.
The White House announced the sweeping round of import duties – due to come into effect next month – on Monday, igniting fresh tensions between Washington and Ottawa.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump defends 50% tariffs on Canada, saying ‘they need us to survive’

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Thousands of people again on the streets of Delhi calling for education reforms despite police violence on Monday
Taru had come to the protest prepared this time. In one hand was an anti-government poster and in the other was a bicycle helmet. “We need to have protection in case Delhi police beat us up again,” said the 25-year-old, who stood among her friends. “We are not scared of them and we won’t run away, no matter what they do. We’ll stay here till they listen.”
On Tuesday, central Delhi still thronged with thousands of protesters, as an unprecedented expression of dissent against the powerful ruling Narendra Modi government showed no sign of abating.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: India’s Cockroach movement protesters show no sign of backing down

articles.author: Associated Press  in Kabul
articles.description:
National disaster agency confirms ‘severe financial and human losses’ in eastern  province of Nuristan
Rescue crews in Afghanistan are searching for survivors and bodies among the rubble of houses destroyed by devastating flash floods that authorities said had killed nearly two dozen people and left more than 100 people missing.
The Afghanistan national disaster management authority said on Tuesday that 23 people had died, 80 had been injured and more than 100 were missing after floods struck the eastern province of Nuristan on Monday, causing an undetermined number of buildings to collapse. The provincial capital city of Parun was among the areas affected, authorities said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rescuers in Afghanistan search for missing and dead after flash floods destroy homes

articles.author: Kat Lay Global health correspondent
articles.description:
Global hunger declined for the third year in a row in 2025 but experts call for action to bring down costs of fruit, vegetables and dairy as report shows 2.69bn people can’t afford to eat well
One in three people cannot afford to eat a healthy diet, a new report has found, prompting calls for urgent action on food affordability.
There are 2.69 billion people unable to afford a diverse diet that meets their energy and nutrient needs, and it will take “immense” amounts of work to achieve the global target of zero hunger by 2030, the annual report from five UN agencies warned.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Healthy diet too expensive for one in three people globally, UN report finds

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Youth-led group calls on education minister to quit in one of India’s largest anti-government rallies in years

Tens of thousands of protesters have defied police orders and descended on Delhi to demand the resignation of India’s education minister in one of the largest anti-government demonstrations in years.
A huge crowd, largely made up of students and gen Z-ers, filled the streets in the heart of India’s capital from early Monday morning shouting anti-government slogans. Hundreds had already camped out overnight.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tens of thousands of Cockroach movement protesters defy police with Delhi march

articles.author: Sarah Basford Canales
articles.description:
Many of the more than 100 people awaiting processing on the tiny Pacific island are skipping meals to make ends meet, a new survey has found

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Most refugees and asylum seekers held in Nauru’s detention centres say they cannot afford to buy enough food or access clean drinking water, despite the Australian government spending the equivalent of more than $9m per person last financial year.
The group of more than 100 people have been sent indefinitely to the tiny Pacific island while they wait for their asylum claims to be processed. Many of the cohort say they are skipping meals to make ends meet, according to a new survey by the Asylum Seeker Resource Centre (ASRC) advocacy group.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia spent more than $9m for each asylum seeker held on Nauru last year – so why can’t they afford to buy food?

articles.author: Carmen Aguilar García and Antonio Voce in London; Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Aakash Hassan in Delhi
articles.description:
Exclusive: Outdoor workers losing up to 9% of income as weather becomes ‘poverty multiplier’, research says
Extreme heat is pushing some of India’s poorest workers further into poverty, with income losses of up to 9% for outdoor workers, new research has found.
Analysis done by the International Institute for Environment and Development (IIED), and shared exclusively with the Guardian, found that extreme heat is acting as a “poverty multiplier” for hundreds of millions of workers in India’s informal sector.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘When I get home, my whole body aches’: extreme heat saps health and wages of India’s poorest workers

articles.author: Eromo Egbejule in Abidjan
articles.description:
Incumbent Carlos Vila Nova hopes to defeat his former party and secure second term as independent
Voters in São Tomé and Príncipe go to the polls for a presidential election on Sunday as one of Africa’s least populous countries seeks to burnish its democratic credentials.
According to the National Election Commission, about 142,000 people are registered to vote in the tiny African state’s elections, approximately 15% of whom live in the diaspora.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: São Tomé and Príncipe heads to polls in tense presidential election

articles.author: Carlos Mureithi in Greater Accra
articles.description:
Hand-painted works are often wildly unfaithful to the movies they portray – reinterpretations that sometimes resulted in threats, insults and even physical attacks from viewers who felt duped
Sitting on his porch in Teshie near Accra, Heavy J dipped a brush into red oil paint and dabbed it carefully on to his canvas – a flour sack – adding blood to a knife being wielded by a man. Higher on the canvas, he had started on an outline of a skull.
Heavy J was creating a poster, but not as you might have expected for a horror film. Instead, it was for the animated fairytale The Little Mermaid. The man with the knife was not a killer but the film’s kind-hearted prince, Eric. The skull was also unrelated to the story. “We add more to make people interested,” said Heavy J, whose real name is Jeaurs Affutu.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘We are preserving a tradition’: how Ghana’s sensationalist film posters became collectible art

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Aid workers are first known people to quarantine at facility, which sparked huge opposition in Kenya 
Seven American aid workers who had been in Congo to fight the Ebola outbreak are quarantining at a new isolation facility in ⁠Kenya after the US government introduced travel ⁠restrictions, the head of a US charity ​employing them told Reuters.
The aid workers are the first known people to quarantine at the facility, which has sparked huge opposition in Kenya and is at the heart of a legal case in which a court has ordered the work to be ⁠suspended. Construction continued, however, according to US officials and satellite imagery reviewed by Reuters.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Seven Americans quarantining at Kenya Ebola facility after US travel ban, says aid group

articles.author: Robert Mackey, Shrai Popat, Lucy Campbell and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

US signs landmark nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia

Sign up for the Breaking News US email

A reminder that my colleagues are covering the latest out of the Middle East at our dedicated live blog.
Donald Trump took to Truth Social a short while and noted that the US will destroy one bridge or power plant, including those near Tehran, “any time” that Iran “shoots a ship” in the strait of Hormuz. 
 Continue reading...
articles.title: House Democrat calls for congressional hearings on Trump administration’s nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia – as it happened

articles.author: Maya Yang and Patrick Wintour
articles.description:
Trump administration hails agreement, which comes as the US fights a war with Iran in part to prevent Tehran enriching uranium domestically
The US has signed a landmark nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia that could allow the kingdom to enrich uranium in the future.
In a statement on Wednesday, the US Department of Energy said its secretary, Chris Wright, and his Saudi counterpart, Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman, signed a “peaceful nuclear cooperation agreement”, along with a “bilateral safeguards agreement”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US signs landmark nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia that could pave the way for domestic nuclear enrichment

articles.author: George Chidi in Marietta, Georgia
articles.description:
President visits swing state to promote ‘Trump accounts’ and says high prices lingering from Joe Biden’s presidency 
Donald Trump scoffed at the word “affordability” as a political message, describing it at a campaign rally on Wednesday as a term concocted by Democratic political consultants to criticize his presidency. Yet even as the president dismissed the notion of affordability, he devoted much of his speech at Wheeler high school to touting the bread-and-butter benefits of his economic policies.
“So I just want you to remember that if you’re paying a little bit more – a lot of it’s come down now, we got it coming down very rapidly actually,” Trump said in Marietta, an Atlanta suburb, casting higher prices today as a lingering effect of the Biden administration.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump scoffs at ‘affordability’ as he touts economic policies at Georgia rally

articles.author: Chris Stein
articles.description:
GOP-controlled chamber paves way for reconciliation bill, while making long-shot attempt at new voting restrictions
House Republicans on Wednesday agreed to begin the process of writing a $95bn bill to fund the war with Iran as well as provide new aid to farmers, while making a long-shot attempt to impose new restrictions on voting nationwide.
In a virtually party-line 216-214, the Republican-controlled chamber passed a budget resolution that paves the way for the creation of a reconciliation bill, which can advance through the Senate under special rules that circumvent the Democratic filibuster and requires only a simple majority to pass. Two Republicans – Warren Davidson of Ohio and Thomas Massie of Kentucky, as well as Kevin Kiley, an independent of California who aligns with the GOP – joined all Democrats in opposing the measure.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: House Republicans to write $95bn bill to fund Iran war and aid farmers

articles.author: Hosted by Kai Wright and Carter Sherman , with David Smith and Rachel Leingang . Produced by Suzanne Gaber and Tiara Chiaramonte , edited by Anabel Bacon , engineered by Ivan Kuraev
articles.description:
Earlier this year, Congress reached a depressing milestone: 86% of Americans, a record high, disapproved of its job performance. But this summer, there have been some signs that shifts are underway. On the left, House Democrats have just voted in unprecedented numbers to withhold military aid from Israel, and across the country, progressive candidates are running competitive primary campaigns that are energizing a base fed up with the status quo. On the right, Republicans are reeling from the sudden death of Lindsay Graham, the South Carolina senator and one of Donald Trump's staunchest supporters. Mitch McConnell, the former Senate majority leader, remains sequestered following a health scare in June, raising questions of if a changing of the guard might be underway there, too. Kai Wright and Carter Sherman are joined by David Smith, the Guardian's Washington bureau chief and Rachel Leingang, midwest political correspondent, to discuss gerontocracy, transparency, the rise of the Democratic Socialists of America and just how much of an inflection point this summer might be for both parties
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Is US Congress finally on the verge of a change? – Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.author: Chris Stein
articles.description:
Passage of annual bill complicated by Trump’s decision to join Israel in attacking Iran without congressional approval
The US House of Representatives passed a $1.15tn defense policy bill in a near-party-line vote on Wednesday, after Democrats refused to back the measure amid the war with Iran and Donald Trump’s push to impose new restrictions on voting nationwide.
A key plank of the president’s plan to spend $1.5tn on the military in the 2027 fiscal year, the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), passed the Republican-controlled chamber by a 216-212 vote, with all but six Democrats opposing its passage. Seven House Republicans broke ranks to oppose the measure, which now goes to the Senate.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: House passes $1.15tn defense bill despite standoff over Israel and Trump’s voter agenda

articles.author: Guardian staff
articles.description:
Late-night host spoke about president’s recent social media posts, including comments on the World Cup and Canada
Seth Meyers discussed Donald Trump’s most recent comments on the World Cup, including his claim that players don’t work hard enough.
On Late Night, the host spoke about a social media post from the US president where he thanked Rudy Giuliani’s son, Andrew, for helping to organise the tournament in the US.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Seth Meyers on Trump calling Canadian wildfire cost incalculable: ‘So he didn’t write that post’

articles.author: Steven Greenhouse
articles.description:
To win in this year’s midterm elections, the party must highlight that Trump has made huge financial gains while millions struggle to make ends meet
If the Democrats hope to maximize their chances of winning in this November’s elections, there’s a subject they need to scream far and wide about: Donald Trump’s immense and unprecedented corruption. The Democrats need to make clear to every American that Trump has shamelessly used his second term to increase his wealth by an astounding amount – by more than $2bn – all while millions of Americans are struggling to make ends meet, their struggles made worse by Trump policies that have pushed up inflation and gas prices.
Every day through election day, the Democrats should convey loud and clear that America’s billionaire president has focused far more on making himself richer than on improving the lives of average Americans. Trump’s corruption and conflicts of interest are so vast and outrageous that many Americans have little idea how vast and outrageous they are: ranging from Trump’s making more than $1.4bn from crypto last year to granting pardons to criminals whose families have donated to Trump’s campaign to his sons’ investing in startup companies that receive generous help from the Trump administration.
Steven Greenhouse is a journalist and author, focusing on labor and the workplace, as well as economic and legal issues
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Democrats need to hammer Trump on his unprecedented corruption | Steven Greenhouse

articles.author: Robert B Shpiner
articles.description:
Stephen Miller warned of a leftwing ‘cancer’ threatening civilization. As a critical care doctor, I have a response to his diagnosis
The presumption that US elections are legitimate died last week in Washington. It was 237 years old. It did not die of one wound. It died of three, inflicted in a single day, in daylight, on the record. And the country, running to the loudest of them, never examined the one most likely to kill.
In critical care we distinguish the mechanism of death from its cause. The mechanism was a Thursday. The cause was chronic, progressive and untreated.
Robert B Shpiner is a clinical professor of medicine in pulmonary and critical care at the David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Three speeches on a single day signaled a dying American democracy | Robert Shpiner

articles.author: Andrew Gumbel in Los Angeles
articles.description:
After ICE raids and protest crackdown, the LA team’s supporters are ambivalent about the World Series winners’ visit
Like many children of Latino immigrants in Los Angeles, Juan grew up a Dodgers fan. He watched their baseball games from home when he was little – even though his parents, who are Guatemalan, were more interested in soccer and basketball – and has been to Dodger Stadium many times as an adult. He sports a Dodgers logo, among other symbols, on an elaborate tattoo on his left forearm.
These days, though, he’s not sure about his allegiance. Juan – whom the Guardian is only identifying by his first name amid the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown – saw his family ripped apart when his father, who had been in the US for close to 30 years, was plucked off the street last year and deported. From that moment on, a team that many immigrants in LA see as a symbol of integration and belonging became, for him, an organization unwilling to stand up for its large immigrant fanbase.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: As Dodgers head to White House, loyal fans are conflicted: ‘Trump is tearing this city apart’

articles.author: Sam Levin and Sophie Sullivan in Los Angeles
articles.description:
Nearly all car ‘assault’ cases promoted by DHS in press releases have been disproven or dropped, a Guardian analysis of court records reveals
The Trump administration has repeatedly accused immigrants and protesters of “weaponizing” their vehicles to “assault” federal immigration agents, a claim used to justify arrests and deadly shootings by officers.
But a Guardian review of 26 cases that the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has promoted as evidence of a surge in “vehicular attacks” reveals most of those claims have fallen apart under scrutiny, with the accusations consistently disproven by evidence or rejected in court. Only one of the 26 cases has resulted in an assault conviction, according to court records and information shared by prosecutors.
Fifteen of the 26 people accused of vehicle attacks never faced federal criminal charges over the incidents, and 11 of the 26 people did.
Eight people who were charged had their cases dismissed, including one person who received a “deferred prosecution”, meaning charges will be dropped if the defendant meets certain conditions.
One person has a pending assault charge; one pleaded guilty to assault; and one was convicted of “destruction of government property”, but acquitted of assault.
DHS has repeatedly continued to promote people’s cases as evidence of violence long after the original claims fell apart.
Cases were dropped or never charged in California, Colorado, Arizona, Illinois, Minnesota, North Carolina, Maryland and Washington DC.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ICE keeps accusing immigrants of ‘weaponizing’ vehicles. Most claims fall apart

articles.author: Arwa Mahdawi
articles.description:
Once Republicans’ favourite punchline, Joe Biden’s son is now building an online following by trolling JD Vance, taunting Trump and embracing the absurdity of US politics
What sort of longshot candidate do we reckon is going to run for US president in 2028? The Rock? Kim Kardashian? Kermit the Frog? US politics has become so debased that being rich, famous and a natural-born citizen (sorry, Zohran Mamdani) now seem to be the only qualifications required for a job in the White House.
Which is why you shouldn’t entirely write off murmurings that Hunter Biden might be interested in following in his daddy’s presidential footsteps. When asked by a Fox News reporter about Hunter’s 2028 odds last month, Donald Trump suggested Joe Biden’s prodigal son might “do well”. If other “basket case[s]” in the Democratic party could do well, Trump added, then Hunter probably had a shot. Various analysts appear to agree. “Could Hunter Biden run for office? Don’t rule it out,” a recent Times headline blared. The article quotes a Biden biographer saying: “With a character like Hunter Biden in a populist, social media-driven political environment, you have to never say never.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hunter Biden for president? Stranger things have happened | Arwa Mahdawi

articles.author: George Chidi in Memphis
articles.description:
The city rallied behind Tamboli’s despite online boycott calls, as frustration grows over the Trump administration’s federal taskforce following multiple deaths
You can measure the disconnect between angry internet commentariat and real life Memphis residents by the length of the wait for a table at Tamboli’s Pasta & Pizza.
In early July, Miles Tamboli, the owner of the midtown pizza spot, made a decision: he would not serve the national guard deployed to the city by the Trump administration, which the US president claimed would reduce the city’s crime rate. Tamboli’s video announcement came days after troops killed two city residents, bringing the total to four since the initiative started in September.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Buy-cott’ boosts Memphis pizza shop after owner refuses to serve national guard

articles.author: Bhaskar Sunkara
articles.description:
The congresswoman can run a serious national campaign on the left and pull a movement in behind it. She should get in early
In the summer of 2018, almost no one thought Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez could beat Joe Crowley. Crowley was a 10-term incumbent, the fourth-ranking Democrat in the House, a man some thought would one day be speaker. A 28-year-old former bartender and democratic socialist was the longest of long shots to succeed him. But ever since she did, the political establishment has been trying to decide whether to take her seriously.
For a while it decided not to. The Missouri representative Emanuel Cleaver said the Democratic caucus did not need her “sniping”, while the then senator Claire McCaskill dismissed her as a “bright and shiny new object”. Ocasio-Cortez seemed to enjoy the response. Asked on 60 Minutes whether she wanted people to underestimate her, she said: “Absolutely. That’s how I won my primary.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez should run for president | Bhaskar Sunkara

articles.author: Sam Levine Zhara Keogh Michael Kalenderian Sarah Bertram
articles.description:
Donald Trump delivered a primetime address to the country on Thursday, claiming that declassified intelligence showed Chinese interference in US elections. The US president revived long-running attacks on election security, despite a US intelligence assessment that found no evidence Beijing altered the 2020 vote, which he lost. The Guardian's voting rights reporter Sam Levine factchecks some of Trump's claims

Trump is invoking foreign election interference to justify his own - Opinion

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fact-checking Donald Trump’s address on Chinese election interference – video

articles.author: Hosted by Jonathan Freedland . Produced by May Robson, Jacob Liebenberg, Ned Carter Miles and the executive producer is Maz Ebtehaj .
articles.description:
The debate about how old is too old to serve in public office has resurfaced this week after the shock death of the Republican senator Lindsey Graham and the surprise return of Mitch McConnell, the 84-year-old senator who published a photo of himself in hospital after a long absence from the spotlight.
With rumours continuing to swirl around Donald Trump’s health, why is it US politicians seem to cling on to power for so long?
Jonathan Freedland speaks to Alexis Coe, a presidential historian and columnist for the New York Times Book review, about whether the US is becoming a gerontocracy – and what can be done about it
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Are American politicians too old? | Politics Weekly America

articles.author: Hosted by Kai Wright and Carter Sherman , with Shrai Popat and Lauren Gambino . Produced by Meg Driscoll, edited by Anabel Bacon , engineered by Ivan Kuraev
articles.description:
Earlier this week, Graham Platner, the Democratic candidate for Senate in Maine, was accused by a former partner of sexual assault. Platner denies the allegations, but on Wednesday, he suspended his campaign, accusing the “political establishment” of tanking his candidacy. But this is only the most recent scandal to have surfaced around Platner’s campaign — over the past year, the oyster farmer and combat veteran was revealed to have a tattoo that closely resembled a Totenkopf (a widely recognized Nazi symbol), a long paper trail of racist, misogynist and homophobic posts on Reddit, and in June, the New York Times published allegations from three former partners about Platner’s “toxic” behavior in their relationships, including, in several cases, physical intimidation (allegations Platner denied).
As Democrats regroup and evaluate their dwindling chances to flip the Senate in November, hosts Kai Wright and Carter Sherman are joined by Guardian political reporters Lauren Gambino and Shrai Popat to ask why voters flocked to Platner, why they were reluctant to abandon him as the scandals came out — and what the whole mess says about who gets the privilege of political redemption.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why Graham Platner wasn’t the answer to the Democrats’ man problem – Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.author: Aamna Mohdin and Jayni Makwana
articles.description:
More than 70 attacks have been recorded over past year, including acts of violence, property damage and vandalism
One mosque is attacked in Britain every five days, according to new data released by the government’s partner for monitoring anti-Muslim hatred.
More than 70 attacks on mosques in the UK have been recorded over the past year, which include acts of intimidation, violence, property damage, harassment, anti-Muslim hate speech, online abuse and vandalism.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: One UK mosque attacked ‘every five days’, says British Muslim Trust

articles.author: Robyn Vinter
articles.description:
New prime minister has made Sarwar – the first senior Labour figure to call for Keir Starmer’s resignation – a peer
Scottish Labour’s rivals in Holyrood have slammed Anas Sarwar’s shock decision to resign as leader to sit in Andy Burnham’s new government, calling him a “chancer” and accusing him of lying to voters.
The prime minister has made Sarwar – who was the first senior Labour figure to call for Keir Starmer to resign – a peer and given him a ministerial post at the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade, No 10 announced on Wednesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Scottish Labour’s rivals decry ‘chancer’ Anas Sarwar for resigning to join Andy Burnham’s government

articles.author: Hayden Vernon
articles.description:
European Commission says Paramount Skydance’s decision to end Universal venture addresses merger concerns
Paramount Skydance’s £80bn takeover of Warner Brothers took a step closer to being realised after it won conditional approval from the European Union.
The European Commission said Paramount’s offer to ⁠end a film ⁠distribution ​joint venture with Universal Pictures addressed its concerns over the potential merger. As part of its commitments in the EU, Paramount has 13 months from the date of closing the deal to pull out from the venture.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Paramount’s £80bn takeover of Warner Brothers a step closer after EU approval

articles.author: Rajeev Syal and Alexandra Topping
articles.description:
PM says he wants to ensure ‘everything has been looked at’ amid outrage at policy from family of PC Andrew Harper
Andy Burnham is immersed in a deepening political row after ordering a review of plans for the early release of thousands of killers, rapists and sex offenders from prison in September.
After the family of PC Andrew Harper expressed outrage that his killers may be eligible for release, the prime minister responded by pledging to make sure that “everything has been looked at again” before a fresh tranche of about 6,000 offenders were freed on tags.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham stirs up political row with review of release plans for violent criminals

articles.author: Jamie Grierson and Kim Willsher
articles.description:
Public prosecutor for the region said suspect had been initially arrested shortly after the murder on 29 April last year
A 70-year-old woman has been charged with the murder of Karen Carter, the British expat found dead in south-western France last year.
The woman was charged on 2 July with Carter’s murder in Trémolat, in the Dordogne, and is “under judicial supervision”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Woman, 70, charged with murder of British expat Karen Carter in France

articles.author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
articles.description:
Party chair queries status of funds Reform leader received from crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne 
The Conservatives have asked HMRC to investigate whether Nigel Farage should have paid tax on the £5m gift he received from the crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne.
The party chair, Kevin Hollinrake, wrote to the tax authorities questioning whether it was a payment to compensate him for running to be an MP.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tories ask HMRC to investigate whether Nigel Farage owes tax on £5m gift

articles.author: Kiran Stacey and Alexandra Topping
articles.description:
New PM’s conversational tone is markedly different to his predecessor’s, but carries risk of sowing confusion
Before he became Britain’s prime minister, Andy Burnham promised to “do politics differently”. Just three days into his time in Downing Street, that approach is already being put to the test.
In the last two days, the prime minister has been accused of performing U-turns over raising the income tax threshold, raising taxes for higher earners and freezing private sector rents.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘He knows what he’s doing’: Burnham’s off-the-cuff remarks inspire headlines and headaches

articles.author: Joanna Partridge
articles.description:
UK warehouse landlord says board unanimous in recommendation to accept ‘best and final offer’  
The board of the UK warehouse landlord Segro has U-turned and said it would be willing to accept a £14bn takeover by Segro’s bigger US rival, Prologis, in a deal that would be one of the largest foreign takeovers of a UK-listed company.
In the latest blow to the troubled London stock market, Segro said in a statement that its board had “unanimously concluded” it would recommend its shareholders accept what Prologis called its “best and final offer”, made just hours before a deadline.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Segro board U-turns on £14bn takeover bid by US rival Prologis

articles.author: Sandra Laville
articles.description:
Former CEO Matthew Wright and three other ex-employees named in criminal proceedings by Environment Agency
The former chief executive of Southern Water is being prosecuted for conspiracy to defraud along with three other former employees, over allegations they manipulated sewage wastewater testing results to avoid tens of millions of pounds in fines.
Matthew Wright is the first water industry boss to face a criminal charge over sewage discharges. He and three others are charged with conspiracy to defraud the Environment Agency and ​the water regulator, Ofwat, between 2012 and 2017 by ⁠creating artificial “no-flow” ​events ​at wastewater treatment ​works to ​influence ‌compliance checks.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ex-Southern Water boss to face trial over allegedly manipulating sewage testing

articles.author: Alexandra Topping Political correspondent
articles.description:
Victims of crime say it’s ‘no laughing matter’ after ministers caught on hot mic ‘ribbing’ about scheme
Victims of crime have accused ministers of making “cheap jokes” about releasing prisoners early after Wes Streeting and Shabana Mahmood were caught on camera “ribbing” about the scheme.
In a video, the new justice secretary, Alex Norris, can be seen walking towards Mahmood and Streeting, the new defence secretary, who can be heard calling Norris “the enemy now”, while Mahmood responds “no he’s not”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mahmood and Streeting accused of making ‘cheap jokes’ about prisoner early release scheme

articles.author: Hayden Vernon (now); Taz Ali and Tom Ambrose (earlier)
articles.description:
New PM says the main perpetrator in the killing of PC Andrew Harper will now ‘not be subject to early release’ and he will also review ‘whole policy’
Wes Streeting said the US president was “right” to demand Europe pays more for its own defence.
Donald Trump has been increasingly critical of Europe for relying too much on the US for its security, and has demanded Nato allies reach 5% of GDP on defence spending by 2035.
President Trump has called on Europe to carry a greater share of the burden for our own defence, and he is right to do so. The UK has always been a leading light on defence spending, but the world is changing and in these dangerous uncertain times it is clear that we have needed to go further.
That’s why we’ve committed £298bn over the next four years, including an additional £15bn on top of last year’s spending review settlement. At the recent Nato summit, all members reaffirmed our commitment to 3.5 by 35 [3.5% of GDP by 2035].
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK politics: Burnham to review early prisoner release scheme – as it happened

articles.author: Kiran Stacey Policy editor
articles.description:
Proposal ‘throws global south countries under the bus’, says ActionAid UK director

Burnham announces bus fares to be capped at £2


The world’s most vulnerable people will be put at risk by Andy Burnham’s decision to use the aid budget to pay for cheaper bus fares in England, charities have said.
The prime minister announced on Wednesday that he would reduce the fare cap from £3 a journey to £2 next year, funded mainly by changing international climate donations into repayable loans.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Funding bus fare cap from aid budget will hit world’s poorest, Burnham told

articles.author: Peter Apps and Robert Booth
articles.description:
Exclusive: Guardian investigation of CT Group uncovers practice that appears to seek hidden influence over public opinion
A political lobbying firm founded by the former electoral strategist for David Cameron and Boris Johnson secretly pays journalists to write pieces for British newspapers that are favourable to its clients, a Guardian investigation can reveal.
In a practice that appears to create a backdoor for private companies to influence public opinion, lobbyists for CT Group – co-founded by the campaign strategist Lynton Crosby – told an undercover reporter they had paid journalists to place apparently independent stories in newspapers.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lobbying giant filmed offering reporter payment for flattering client coverage in national press

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor
articles.description:
Defence secretary says he will give arms industry ‘clarity and confidence’ in contrast to row preceding Starmer’s exit
Wes Streeting has said increased defence spending would make “an enormous contribution” to economic growth, as he emphasised that the military will be a spending priority for Andy Burnham’s government over other departments.
The new defence secretary, in a speech at the Farnborough airshow, did not make any extra financial commitments, but promised he would give the arms industry “clarity and confidence” in contrast to the row that contributed to the fall of Keir Starmer.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Streeting says Burnham government will prioritise military over other spending

articles.author: Joanna Partridge
articles.description:
Record June temperatures expected to cut grain harvest by 9m tonnes to its lowest level since 2018 
The heatwave that swept across Europe in June is estimated to have cost the continent’s grain farmers €2bn (£1.7bn) in lost revenue and destroyed 9m tonnes of crops, sparking concern about the impact on the price of food.
Coceral, the European cereals and oilseeds trade association, made the estimate for the harvest of crops such as wheat, barley, maize and oats following the heatwave.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Food price fears after Europe’s heatwave destroys estimated €2bn of crops

articles.author: Dan Milmo and Mark Sweney
articles.description:
Bloomsbury has 14,087 titles listed in agreement between AI startup and authors over use of their work 
The publisher of Harry Potter has received a multimillion-pound payout as a beneficiary of a $1.5bn (£1.12bn) copyright settlement between the AI startup Anthropic and thousands of authors over the use of their protected work to power chatbots.
Bloomsbury, which is home to the bestselling novelists Sarah J Maas and Susanna Clarke as well as JK Rowling, said it had 14,087 titles listed within the settlement, with a proposed compensation of about $3,000 a title.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Harry Potter publisher to receive millions in Anthropic copyright settlement

articles.author: Neha Gohil Midlands correspondent
articles.description:
Trust that treated Valdo Calocane, who killed three people in 2023, sectioned him four times between 2020 and 2022
The NHS trust that treated the triple killer Valdo Calocane in the years before the Nottingham attacks is being investigated by police for corporate manslaughter.
Calocane, who has paranoid schizophrenia, was sentenced to an indefinite hospital order after he fatally stabbed the 19-year-old students Barnaby Webber and Grace O’Malley Kumar, and the 65-year-old caretaker Ian Coates, on 13 June 2023.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: NHS trust investigated for corporate manslaughter after Nottingham attacks

articles.author: Lanre Bakare Arts and culture correspondent
articles.description:
Clear frontrunner leaves lucrative role at New York’s Dia Art Foundation to join  UK arts organisation at critical juncture
Jessica Morgan has been confirmed as the new director of Tate, marking her return to the arts organisation where she worked as a curator for more than a decade, at a critical juncture in its history.
Morgan, the clear frontrunner in the race to replace Maria Balshaw, who left this spring after nine years in charge, is currently based in New York, where she has led the Dia Art Foundation since 2015.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Jessica Morgan named new Tate director – with ‘big pay cut’ to take job

articles.author: Kalyeena Makortoff Banking correspondent
articles.description:
John Neal failed to disclose ties with colleague that created a potential conflict of interest, investigation finds
Lloyd’s of London has ruled that its former boss John Neal breached compliance rules by failing to disclose a “close relationship” with a female colleague that risked triggering conflict of interest concerns at the insurance market.
An investigation by the Council of Lloyd’s, which is responsible for the market’s management and supervision, said it could not find any “conclusive evidence” Neal was romantically involved with the company’s then corporate affairs director, nor that there were any process failures relating to her promotion during Neal’s tenure.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lloyd’s of London says ex-boss’s ‘close relationship’ breached compliance rules

articles.author: Kalyeena Makortoff
articles.description:
Pub chain blames worse-than-expected sales on rising costs for workers, food, energy and property taxes
JD Wetherspoon has issued its fourth profit warning in seven months, with the pub chain blaming worse-than-expected sales, despite the World Cup, as it struggled with rising costs for food, workers, energy and property taxes.
Shares in the pub chain tumbled as much as 10% on Wednesday as its chair, Tim Martin, said profits would fall short of forecasts when it reports full-year earnings in October.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Wetherspoon issues fourth profit warning in seven months

articles.author: Anna Bawden Health and social affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Exclusive: Research shows millions live more than a 1km round trip from 24/7 accessible device
More than 16 million people in England and Wales risk dying from a cardiac arrest because they live farther than a 1km round trip from the nearest 24/7 defibrillator, according to exclusive research.

 Analysis of publicly available defibrillators by the Heart Restart campaign found that in England and Wales alone, 35 million people – more than half the population – do not live within the recommended three- to five-minute brisk walk of a defibrillator. Of these, about half live more than a 1km round trip from a 24/7 accessible defibrillator.
There are more than 40,000 out-of-hospital cardiac arrests each year in the UK, but fewer than one in 10 people survive. However, early cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and defibrillation can more than double the chance of survival.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: More than 16m at risk of death by cardiac arrest in England and Wales due to ‘defibrillator deserts’

articles.description:
A rare glimpse of a young puffin emerging from its nest has given conservationists fresh hope for the future of Dorset’s dwindling puffin population. The ‘puffling’ was spotted by volunteers working with the National Trust, who renewed their monitoring efforts at the site in March 2026 to understand why mainland England’s last breeding colony on the south coast was failing to produce chicks. It is the first time in 30 years a puffling sighting has been confirmed at the colony. 

‘A great thrill’: baby puffin is first one seen on Dorset coast in three decades

 Continue reading...
articles.title: First ‘puffling’ sighting in three decades give hope for Dorset's struggling puffin colony – video

articles.author: Steven Morris
articles.description:
Puffling excites volunteers trying to save the last known regular nesting site on mainland of southern England
For years, volunteers have craned their necks and tested their patience to peer into the crevices of the cliffs hoping for a glimpse of fluffy joy.
Finally it all paid off as a puffling – baby puffin – poked its way into the sunshine, becoming the first to be spotted on the coast of Dorset in southern England for three decades.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘A great thrill’: baby puffin is first one seen on Dorset coast in three decades

articles.author: Nadeem Badshah
articles.description:
UK resident was evacuated from Democratic Republic of the Congo where there is an outbreak of the disease
A humanitarian worker is being monitored at a specialist hospital in London after potential exposure to the Ebola virus.
The UK resident was medically evacuated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) where the worker had been treating patients with the disease, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Health worker monitored for Ebola in London hospital after working in DRC

articles.author: Source: Reuters
articles.description:
The prime minister told his new cabinet in its first meeting that the government will be a 'cost-of-living government' and needs to examine 'all possible ways' to help families struggling with high costs. The new prime minister announced an £850m tax cut on electricity bills in his first significant policy announcement
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Andy Burnham to cut tax on electricity to ease cost of living - video

articles.author: Damian Carrington Environment editor
articles.description:
A ‘reasonable worst-case scenario’ suggests need for large-scale movement of populations away from reshaped coast
Up to 13 million people in the UK face the long-term risk of coastal flooding due to the climate crisis, scientists have warned, with a “reasonable worst-case scenario” suggesting the need for the large-scale movement of populations away from a dramatically reshaped coast.
Even if today’s global pledges to cut carbon pollution are met, about 1.4 million more people will be exposed to coastal floods in 2200 and 1.7 million in 2300 due to the sea level rise driven by melting ice caps and warming oceans.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Millions face long-term coastal flooding risk in UK without climate action, scientists warn

articles.author: Ian Sample Science editor
articles.description:
Durham University researchers find cataclysmic direct hit with Gaia Sausage sent Milky Way into its current position
Astronomers have found evidence that the Milky Way was flipped on its side following a direct hit from a wayward galaxy long before the solar system was born.
The cataclysmic collision took place about 10bn years ago when the Milky Way was struck head-on by an incoming dwarf galaxy known – for purely astronomical reasons – as the Gaia Sausage.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Milky Way flipped in collision with dwarf galaxy 10bn years ago, astronomers say

articles.author: Hilary Osborne and Jillian Ambrose
articles.description:
New prime minister is implementing immediate tax cut to help ease cost of living pressures for British households

Andy Burnham to cut VAT on electricity bills as first cost of living move

Household electricity bills for people in Great Britain will not attract VAT for six months, under the first of a series of cost of living measures announced by the new prime minister, Andy Burnham.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: What will Andy Burnham’s VAT cut on electricity bills mean for you?

articles.author: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels and Lisa O’Carroll in London
articles.description:
European leaders have made positive noises about the new UK PM, but he is likely to face the same restrictions as Starmer
Andy Burnham is unknown in Brussels, but that will soon change. In his schedule for the autumn is an EU-UK summit that may underscore the same dilemmas that have confronted previous British prime ministers in the relationship with Europe.
EU leaders were quick to offer congratulations to Britain’s prime minister, the seventh since the 2016 Brexit referendum. The European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, said she looked forward to strengthening the EU-UK partnership “for the security of our shared continent” and “the prosperity of people on both sides of the Channel”. The German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, invited Burnham to visit Berlin “very soon”, noting that the UK and Germany’s “deep connection is particularly evident in these times”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: What the EU wants from Andy Burnham

articles.author: Damien Gayle
articles.description:
Millions of people in southern England and parts of Wales face restrictions after prolonged periods of hot weather
Millions of people across southern England are subject to hosepipe bans after prolonged periods of extreme heat and reduced rainfall. On Tuesday, Thames Water, Britain’s biggest water company, announced a ban starting on Thursday. Here, the Guardian answers questions about what the restriction means for you.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How can I water my garden in a hosepipe ban and will there be drought this summer?

articles.author: Rowena Mason and Peter Walker
articles.description:
From the Treasury to the Home Office, we look at who is heading up key departments in new PM’s government

Burnham vows his arrival in power will be ‘circuit breaker’ moment for UK

Six highlights from Andy Burnham’s first Downing Street speech

Andy Burnham has appointed his first cabinet, with the new prime minister rewarding those who have been loyal to his takeover efforts. He had promised to pick his top team from all wings of the party in an effort to show he is trying to run a more inclusive administration.
But at the same time, his decision to have a brutal clearout of Starmer allies resulted in many considered to be on the right of the party or close to the former prime minister losing their jobs. These are the key announcements so far:
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Andy Burnham’s first Labour cabinet: who’s in and who’s out?

articles.author: Presented by Helen Pidd with Peter Walker and Paul Harrison; produced by Ruth Abrahams, Guy Szafman, Belinda Gurung and Rudi Zygadlo; the executive producer is Sami Kent
articles.description:
Senior political correspondent Peter Walker and former No 10 press secretary Paul Harrison analyse Andy Burnham’s first day as PM
On Monday, Andy Burnham finally realised his long-held ambition to become prime minister. But what problems can he expect to confront now he’s in No 10?
Former Downing Street press secretary Paul Harrison talks through the challenges of the office, from the awkward living arrangements to the even more awkward conversations with the president of the US. And senior political correspondent Peter Walker tells Helen Pidd about Burnham’s first speech at Downing Street, his new cabinet, and what it tells us about his plans in power.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham begins: what awaits the new British PM? - podcast

articles.author: Mark Brown North of England correspondent
articles.description:
Revamped Ripon attraction reopens as a more immersive experience telling ‘national story’ of poverty and welfare
Visitors to one of Britain’s most complete surviving Victorian workhouses won’t have to strip and bathe in someone else’s bath water. But they might get some gruel, they can sweep the yard and there are “schoolmaster” volunteers happy to tell children how to behave.
“You are literally going to walk in the footsteps of people who have experienced this place,” said the director of the Ripon Museums Trust, Alexa Vernon.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Gruel and graft: museum asks if you could survive a Victorian workhouse

articles.author: Pippa Neill Environment reporter
articles.description:
Industry says government’s failure to address cooling demands means AI growth plans are ‘fatally flawed’
The UK will not have enough water for future datacentres, the water industry has said in stark criticism of the government’s AI growth plans.
Datacentres rely on large amounts of water to manage the heat generated by densely packed servers. Cooling towers, chillers and humidification systems make direct use of this water, with large volumes also consumed indirectly through high electrical power needs.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Not enough water for UK’s datacentre plans, trade body says

Senior political correspondent Peter Walker and former No 10 press secretary Paul Harrison analyse Andy Burnham’s first day as PM
On Monday, Andy Burnham finally realised his long-held ambition to become prime minister. But what problems can he expect to confront now he’s in No 10?
Former Downing Street press secretary Paul Harrison talks through the challenges of the office, from the awkward living arrangements to the even more awkward conversations with the president of the US.
